source.name: Theorems about the definitions of the features that measure partials against a fundamental, checked by Lean
source.how: each expected value is proved to be the value of the feature's definition at the doubles nearest the stored values, or within half a unit in its last place of it, by the theorem its record names in spec/XtractSpec/Records/Harmonicity.lean; written by tests/reference/generate/lean_harmonicity.py and checked by Lean's kernel

tolerance.reason: 2 roundings, each within 2^-53 relatively: the division; every amplitude and every frequency is a multiple of 1/4 and the fundamental is a whole number, so each product, each difference and each addition before it is exact; and the expected value

300 roundings, each within 2^-53 relatively: the product of a harmonic number and the fundamental in every term, whose rounding is a part of that product, and those products weighted as the terms are sum to 94.1 times the sum of the terms; the difference, the square of the amplitude and their product, in every term, and the P - 1 additions of the terms of the P partials, in any order; the square of every amplitude and the P - 1 additions of the squares, in any order; the product of the fundamental and that sum; the division; and the expected value

2 roundings, each within 2^-53 relatively: the division; every coefficient is a multiple of 1/4, so each addition is exact, and the library places every peak as the definition does; and the expected value

200 roundings, each within 2^-53 relatively: the library places every peak as the definition does; at most P - 1 additions of the coefficients that are not kept, and the P - 1 additions of the coefficients of the P peaks, each of one sign, in any order; the division; and the expected value
